title: What If Quantum Computers Broke Online Encryption?

scenes.text: What if quantum computers broke the internet's locks? The math has existed since 1994.
That year, mathematician Peter Shor designed an algorithm that factors huge numbers far faster than any normal computer.
Most online security, called RSA, relies on factoring being painfully slow.
A powerful enough quantum machine could break RSA and elliptic curve encryption, which have protected digital identities for nearly 50 years.
That machine doesn't exist yet. But in August 2024, the US standards agency NIST finalized three quantum-resistant standards.
The race isn't to build the lock-breaker. It's to replace every old lock first.

description:
